Resequencer

Local waveform bar sequencing, tempo and key analysis: algorithmic BPM (spectral-flux onsets → autocorrelation + DP beat tracking) and key (tuned chroma → key profiles). Files scan automatically when added. Everything runs locally; nothing is uploaded.
Import settings
Drop MP3 / Ogg / FLAC / WAV files or folders here
Files 0 Done 0 Wall – Throughput – Speed – (track time ÷ wall time) Decode – Analysis – Tag agreement –
#FileDur BPMAlternatesConf KeyRunner-upConf Tag BPMTag keyMatch Decode msAnalyse msStatus
Beat detection · onset strength
Onset strength (log-mel spectral flux) over the analysed excerpt, with tracked beats (orange).
Tempo score
Tempo score vs BPM: harmonic-comb autocorrelation (grey) × log-Gaussian prior (blue); shaded = allowed range.
Key chroma
Chroma (pitch-class energy) after tuning correction; detected key's scale highlighted.

Waveform → bars → sequence

No track selected

Files scan automatically on upload. Click a bar or beat in the waveform to toggle it and immediately loop all selected slices in waveform order. Shift-click adds a range; deselecting the last slice stops. Split any bar into individually selectable beats; rejoin to restore its whole-bar view. Explicit Play remains available. Scroll the single-row slice panel with touch, trackpad or its arrow controls. Playback reveals each new active slice without moving the page. Short slices snap into view; longer slices scroll smoothly, so fast loops do not chase unfinished scroll animations. Sequences are per track and kept for this session only.

Add audio files above to get started.

Beat detection does not identify musical downbeats and can lock onto offbeats. Automatic bar 1 starts on the first consensus grid beat, not a recognised musical downbeat. Check the orange bar lines by ear and adjust the downbeat. Waveform starts fitted to each new file. Mousewheel over the waveform zooms at the pointer; Shift-wheel or horizontal trackpad scroll pans. Use Zoom, Fit, scrollbar or Pan buttons too. Fit to selected shows every selected region in one bounding interval with padding, including the timeline between discontiguous selections; it does not cut out intervening audio. Playback never forces the main waveform to recenter. This is a constant-tempo grid, extrapolated outside the analysed excerpt; variable-tempo recordings may drift. Changing the grid clears this track’s sequence.

Drag any orange divider to slide every grid divider together. BPM and beats per bar stay exactly unchanged; use Grid BPM to change tempo. File edges stay fixed, clipping partial bars as the grid moves. The stored offset is an equivalent phase within one bar. If a short file has no internal divider, use the downbeat offset field. Dragging stops playback; releasing clears the sequence. Esc cancels without clearing. Snap is on by default: the dragged target and shared audio cuts seek low-energy crossings within ±4 ms; the ideal grid remains uniform. Stereo crossings may not be jointly zero; absent crossings stay sample-aligned.

1×Full track

Sequence

Click the background, padding or waveform of a sequence step to play from that step through the rest of the sequence; ▶ Play sequence still starts at the beginning. A green play bar shows progress on the active card and always moves left→right across the displayed (mirrored when reversed) waveform. Text and −/+/Reverse/Remove stay usable and do not start playback. Drag those same non-text areas to reorder after a short movement threshold. Keyboard: focus the card, Enter/Space plays from it, Left/Right or Home/End reorder. Reverse toggles backward playback for that step, including its repeats. Use −/+ to set repeats (1–32), or remove a step as needed. Playback uses original audio, with no time stretching. Short edge bars/beats are marked “partial”. Split/rejoin stops playback and preserves queued sequence cuts; rejoining selected beats selects their whole bar.

Download audio
Save sequence writes a JSON project (cuts, grid, palettes, settings). Audio is not embedded — re-import originals to load. Save sequence audio still renders WAV/Ogg/MP3.
Exports run locally, offline, from a snapshot of the sequence, with repeats/reverse and the same 2 ms edge ramps as sequence playback. WAV preserves float PCM; Ogg/MP3 are lossy. Space pauses/resumes music when not editing a control.
Audio encoder/decoder credits, licenses and replacement

Local encoders: audiojs @audio/encode-mp3 2.0.1 and @audio/encode-ogg 1.3.1, built from wasm-media-encoders 0.7.0 with LAME (www.mp3dev.org), libogg and libvorbis. Local Ogg decoders (fallback when the browser cannot decode): @wasm-audio-decoders/ogg-vorbis 0.1.20 and ogg-opus-decoder 1.7.5 (MIT; Ethan Halsall / wasm-audio-decoders), based on libvorbis/libopus/libogg. All encoder and decoder JavaScript and WASM are embedded; decode and export perform no network requests. No warranty.

Codec sources, exact dependency revisions, licenses and rebuilding instructions accompany this file as resequencer-export-source.zip. Sources: https://github.com/audiojs/encode and https://github.com/arseneyr/wasm-media-encoders/tree/v0.7.0 . To replace/relink encoders, rebuild export-worker.js with your replacement libraries and replace the Base64 contents of the hidden exportWorkerData textarea. The app and editable worker source impose no restriction on modifying or reverse engineering the library integration for debugging such modifications.

@wasm-audio-decoders/ogg-vorbis 0.1.20 and ogg-opus-decoder 1.7.5 (MIT)

Browser WASM fallback decoders used when decodeAudioData cannot decode an Ogg Vorbis or Ogg Opus file (for example in browsers without native Vorbis).
